On Saturday, the town opened a new community garden on an empty lot on Elm Street. The garden has 40 small plots where residents can grow vegetables, herbs, and flowers. Each plot costs $25 for the season, and the town provides water, tools, and free advice from experienced gardeners every Sunday morning. "Many people here live in apartments and don't have a yard," said Linda Hoff, who organized the project. "Now they have a place to grow their own food." Half of the plots were rented on the first day, so people who are interested should apply soon at the town hall. Gardeners may give any extra vegetables to the local food bank.

choices: A cooking class for apartment owners
A new apartment building on Elm Street
A new garden for town residents
explanation: The article describes the new community garden on Elm Street and how residents can use it.

BORROW MORE THAN BOOKS
The Westfield Public Library has started a new service called the Library of Things. In addition to books and movies, members can now borrow everyday items that they may need only once or twice a year, such as tents, sewing machines, camping stoves, and even a small telescope. Items can be borrowed for up to one week at no charge. "Buying something expensive that you hardly ever use doesn't make sense," explained library director Paul Jensen. "Sharing these items saves people money and reduces waste." The library plans to expand the collection based on suggestions from members, and a suggestion form is available at the information desk. Because the items are popular, members are encouraged to reserve them online at least a few days in advance.
stem: What is the article mainly about?
choices: A library that sells used books
A new camping store in Westfield
A library that lends everyday items
A sewing class at the library
explanation: The article describes the library's new service for borrowing items such as tents and sewing machines.

NOW HIRING: PART-TIME MUSEUM GUIDES
The Clearwater History Museum is looking for friendly, reliable people to lead tours for visitors of all ages. Guides work 12 to 15 hours a week, mostly on weekends and during school holidays. No experience is necessary, as all new guides receive two weeks of paid training. However, applicants must be comfortable speaking in front of groups. Knowledge of a second language is a plus, since many of our visitors come from other countries. Guides earn $16 per hour and receive free admission to all museum events for themselves and one guest. To apply, send a short letter explaining why you are interested, along with your résumé, to the museum office by April 30. Interviews will take place during the first week of May.

explanation: The ad says the museum is hiring part-time guides and explains how to apply.
